transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

4C on a Samsung DW60M6050FS means the dishwasher is not detecting an adequate water supply. It will beep and refuse to start to prevent damage.

Try these checks:

1. Reset it
• Turn the dishwasher off at the mains or unplug it for 5 minutes.
• Turn it back on and try a new cycle.

2. Check the water tap
• The dishwasher’s cold-water isolation valve (usually under the sink) must be fully open.
• Check that your kitchen cold tap has normal pressure. If it is weak or off, the dishwasher cannot fill.

3. Inspect the inlet hose
• Pull the machine forward only if safe to do so.
• Make sure the water inlet hose behind it is not kinked, crushed, twisted, or trapped.
• If it has an AquaStop box on the hose, do not try to dismantle that box.

4. Clean the inlet filter
• Turn off the water valve and unplug the dishwasher.
• Unscrew the inlet hose from the water tap.
• There is usually a small mesh filter in the hose connection / dishwasher inlet. Carefully remove debris and rinse it clean.
• Refit it securely, turn the water back on, and check for leaks.

5. Check for a supply issue
• If water has recently been turned off, pipes frozen, or plumbing work done, the dishwasher may need a couple of attempts after the supply is restored.
• Do not use a damaged hose or connection.

If 4C returns immediately even though the tap is open, pressure is good, and the filter/hose are clear, likely causes are a failed inlet valve, faulty AquaStop hose, wiring issue, or control-board fault. That will need a dishwasher engineer/Samsung service.

If you see water leaking, smell burning, or the machine trips electrics, leave it switched off and shut off the water valve.

Did the reset first, same 4C. Then I checked the valve under the sink, the screwdriver-slot one, and the slot was at 90 degrees so it was turned off. I turned it on and the dishwasher now fills and runs normally. No kinks in the hose and the tap pressure is fine. I haven't done the filter.

That explains it: the dishwasher water isolation valve was off. With the slot at 90° to the pipe, it was closed; turning it inline with the pipe opened the supply.

Since it now fills and runs normally, there’s no need to clean the inlet filter at this point. Just keep an eye on the first full cycle for any drips around the valve or hose connection.

The 4C code should not return unless the water supply is interrupted or restricted again.
